lead: Fan-out is an orchestrator releasing N workers on independent items and gathering only what matters. It works when each item fits in a clear request, has a cap, and returns a line you can check. In this lesson you run a shell fan-out with a fake agent, watch the time drop, and redo only the rejected item.
objetivo: run a fan-out with N workers, a cap per item, and a short consolidation, redoing only the rejected item.

aprende.t: The forms of fan-out in Claude Code and in the shell
The delegation request: goal, format, sources, and boundaries
Cap per worker and return in a file
Consolidate by the last line and redo only the rejected one

hero_alt: A thick cable that splits into five thin cables connected to five identical modules with a green LED.

secoes.sub: The orchestrator plans and merges; the workers only do their part. Click each step.

nos.detalhe: In Anthropic's research system, the lead breaks down the question and describes each subtask. A vague request ("research the chip shortage") made three subagents repeat the same search. The rule written in their prompt: simple fact, 1 agent with 3 to 10 calls; comparison, 2 to 4 subagents; complex research, more than 10.
One item per line, with the input already ready. If an item depends on the result of another, it doesn't go in the fan-out: it goes afterward (hybrid, lesson 1).

Each worker receives only its own item, runs with a cap (timeout), and writes the result to a file. In Claude Code, the same idea is asking for several subagents in one message; the limit is 20 running at the same time.

The orchestrator reads the last line of each file (OK or FALHA: reason), not the whole text. Anthropic calls this avoiding the game of telephone: the worker writes the artifact and passes back a lightweight reference.

secoes.volta: Rejected? Only that item goes back on the list; approved ones are not redone
secoes.legenda: A fan-out of 500 mechanical files needs no model at all: it's a script. An agent comes in when each item requires judgment.

secoes.sub: Per the Claude Code docs (Run agents in parallel, read on Oct 19, 2026) and Codex CLI 0.163.0.

texto: Ask for several subagents in the same message. The results come back to the conversation that created them.

For a large, repeatable batch, the docs point to dynamic workflows (a script that runs many subagents and compares their results) and /batch, which splits a large change across 5 to 30 subagents, each in its own worktree.
claude --bg drops a session into the background; claude agents shows them all on one screen. Before editing, the background session moves into its own worktree in .claude/worktrees/.
Each session spends its own quota. Merge the results by file, in a lead session or in a script.

Off by default (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1). A lead and teammates with a task list and messages between them. One team per session, no nested teams, and /resume does not restore in-process teammates.
Teammates don't get a worktree: two editing the same file overwrite each other. Split the files by owner.
Outside the session, an xargs -P with claude -p or codex exec per item. This is the one you control best: cap, output file, resume.
This is the form used in the rehearsal below, because you can swap the agent for a fake script.

secoes.titulo: Fan-out in shell, with a rehearsal
secoes.sub: The AGENTE is any command that reads the request on stdin. For the rehearsal, use a script that sleeps 2 s and answers.

blocos.conteudo:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# fanout.sh — one worker per line of the list, N at a time, short return in a file.
# Usage: fanout.sh <lista.txt> <pasta-saida> [N]
#   AGENTE = command that reads the request on stdin (default: claude -p). For a rehearsal: a fake script.
#   TETO   = seconds per worker (default 600)
set -u
LISTA="${1:?uso: fanout.sh <lista.txt> <pasta-saida> [N]}"; OUT="${2:?pasta de saída}"; N="${3:-3}"
export OUT AGENTE="${AGENTE:-claude -p}" TETO="${TETO:-600}"
mkdir -p "$OUT"

trabalho() {
  item="$1"; nome=$(printf '%s' "$item" | tr -cs 'a-zA-Z0-9' '-' | cut -c1-40)
  if [ -s "$OUT/$nome.md" ] && [ "$(tail -1 "$OUT/$nome.md")" = OK ]; then
    echo "pula $nome (aprovado)"; return 0     # only the rejected one comes back
  fi
  printf 'Task: %s\nAnswer in at most 5 lines. Last line: OK, or FALHA: <reason>.\n' "$item" \
    | timeout "$TETO" $AGENTE > "$OUT/$nome.tmp" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then mv "$OUT/$nome.tmp" "$OUT/$nome.md"; echo "feito $nome"
  else mv "$OUT/$nome.tmp" "$OUT/$nome.erro"; echo "erro $nome (rc=$rc)"; fi
}
export -f trabalho

grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' "$LISTA" | xargs -d '\n' -P "$N" -I{} bash -c 'trabalho "$1"' _ {}

# the orchestrator merges only the last lines: that is what goes back into its context
for f in "$OUT"/*.md; do [ -e "$f" ] && printf '%s: %s\n' "$(basename "$f" .md)" "$(tail -1 "$f")"; done > "$OUT/../consolidado.txt"
echo "itens: $(grep -cv '^[[:space:]]*$' "$LISTA") · feitos: $(ls "$OUT"/*.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l) · com erro: $(ls "$OUT"/*.erro 2>/dev/null | wc -l) · OK: $(grep -c ': OK$' "$OUT/../consolidado.txt") · FALHA: $(grep -c ': FALHA' "$OUT/../consolidado.txt")"

cd ~/treino-multi && chmod +x fanout.sh
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-multi/fanout; rm -rf $E && mkdir -p $E
cat > $E/agente-falso.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
pedido=$(cat); sleep 2
case "$pedido" in
  *quebrado*) printf 'não consegui ler o arquivo\nFALHA: arquivo quebrado\n' ;;
  *) printf 'resumo de uma linha\nOK\n' ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x $E/agente-falso.sh
printf 'resumir docs/a.md\nresumir docs/b.md\nresumir docs/quebrado.md\nresumir docs/c.md\nresumir docs/d.md\n' > $E/lista.txt

time AGENTE=$E/agente-falso.sh ./fanout.sh $E/lista.txt $E/saida 1   # one at a time
rm -rf $E/saida
time AGENTE=$E/agente-falso.sh ./fanout.sh $E/lista.txt $E/saida 3   # three at a time
AGENTE=$E/agente-falso.sh ./fanout.sh $E/lista.txt $E/saida 3        # again: nothing is redone
cat $E/consolidado.txt

A cap is mandatory, but calibrated: run one real item alone, measure it, and leave some slack. Without a cap, one stuck worker holds up the whole batch.

secoes.sub: When the fan-out happens inside the session, you are the orchestrator, making the request. The four fields come from Anthropic's post.

blocos.rot: Prompt · fan-out with subagents in one session
blocos.conteudo:
Split this into subagents, one per item in the list below, all in the same message.
For each subagent, write:
- Goal: <what this item needs to answer>
- Output format: at most 5 lines; last line OK or FALHA: <reason>; write to saida/<item>.md
- Sources and tools: <files or folders it may read>; do not edit anything outside saida/
- Boundary: do not handle the other items; if it depends on another item, stop and say which one
Then read only the last line of each file and give me the item → OK/FALHA table.
Items:
<item 1>
<item 2>
<item 3>

perguntas.p: Why does the orchestrator read only the last line of each result?
opcoes: Because the rest of the output is tool log, which always comes truncated and is useless
To avoid filling its own context: the artifact stays in the file, only the reference comes back
perguntas.explica: It's the same principle as the subagent: the detail stays out. When it needs to, the orchestrator opens only the file of the failed item.

perguntas.p: What was missing from the request that made three Anthropic subagents repeat the same search?
opcoes: A bigger model in the orchestrator, which deduces on its own what each subagent should look for
Objective, output format, sources, and clear boundaries for each subagent
perguntas.explica: With a vague request, each subagent interpreted it in its own way and the work was duplicated. The four fields split up the work.

perguntas.p: In the second round of fanout.sh, who runs again?
opcoes: Only the ones that hit the timeout; the ones that printed FALHA stay as they are
Only the items whose last line is not OK
perguntas.explica: Approved items are not reprocessed. FALHA and .erro come back; this is the rule "only the failed one comes back" from the lesson 1 kit.

perguntas.p: Two teammates in an agent team need to edit the same file. What does the doc recommend?
opcoes: Nothing: the team coordinates itself and each teammate works on its own copy of the repository
Split the work so each teammate owns different files
perguntas.explica: Agent teams don't give each teammate a worktree: editing the same file overwrites it. Partition by owner, or isolation (lesson 5).

itens.texto: Only what doesn't depend on another item goes into the fan-out; the rest goes before or after.
Each worker with a timeout, a saved result, and a last line of OK or FALHA.

itens.t: Only the failed one comes back
itens.texto: The orchestrator reads the last lines and reruns only what failed.
